title: Lauren Tan's agent kitchen: how she scaled to 2,500 PRs
source_label: Matt Pocock interview with Lauren Tan, also known as poteto
caption_provenance: English automatic captions acquired from YouTube. The untouched SRT and JSON are retained in the local research record, outside the public site.

scenes.title: From micromanaging to earned trust
scenes.explanation: Lauren traces pstack to repeated effort supervising one agent and removing herself as the bridge to debugging evidence.

scenes.title: Expertise becomes expressible intent
scenes.explanation: Stronger execution raises the value of domain knowledge, precise goals, and vocabulary that makes hidden requirements explicit.

scenes.title: Why a Michelin kitchen
scenes.explanation: The kitchen metaphor combines throughput with craft and assigns the human responsibility for tools, organization, and final quality.

scenes.title: Verification closes the loop
scenes.explanation: Agents need tools to run the application, observe behavior, compare it with a goal, and revise their work.

scenes.title: Put deterministic work in tools
scenes.explanation: A reusable CLI handles repeatable mechanics while the agent spends judgment on ambiguous decisions and evidence.

scenes.title: Invest in the environment before parallelism
scenes.explanation: Low trust creates a micromanagement cycle, so tools and constraints need deliberate investment before agent count grows.

scenes.title: Dune narrows possible mistakes
scenes.explanation: Lauren uses internal framework conventions, feature directories, and lint rules to reduce the number of invalid implementation paths.

scenes.title: Connect the outer and inner loops
scenes.explanation: External reports must refresh engineering context, while inner-loop agents still reproduce and verify each problem.

scenes.title: Scale projects, not chats
scenes.explanation: Persistent coordinators manage task lists, workers, and shared context instead of multiplying independent chats.

scenes.title: Coordinate with context
scenes.explanation: Grouping related reports before delegation can expose a common root cause and avoid duplicate fixes.

scenes.title: The PR count includes gardening
scenes.explanation: Lauren says much of the reported PR volume is maintenance that improves the environment rather than new features.

scenes.title: Buffer findings to see patterns
scenes.explanation: A recurring scan records findings for later comparison so a systemic fix can replace many reactive patches.

scenes.title: Sample code and repair the process
scenes.explanation: Lauren samples landed work and changes shared rules when several agents repeat the same shortcut.

scenes.title: Overnight autopilot and its cost
scenes.explanation: Multiple verifier agents can test, repair, and merge before human review, at substantial token cost and with remaining coverage limits.

scenes.title: Where autonomy remains unresolved
scenes.explanation: Lauren ties autonomy to verifiability and acknowledges that irreversible or hard-to-check work has no universal solution.

scenes.title: Skills are personal, combinable process
scenes.explanation: Users can combine skill libraries, but should understand, adapt, and verify the processes they carry between projects.

scenes.title: Recall and compact workflow skills
scenes.explanation: Recall compresses repeated context recovery into a workflow, followed by the closing view that stronger models can use shorter process descriptions.
